title: Integrated Budgeting, Contracts, Procurement, and Revenue Recognition Policy (Q1 2026)
author: Priya Shah
content:
Summary:
This document defines Redwood Inference’s integrated policy for budgeting and forecasting, contracts and legal approvals, procurement procedures, and revenue recognition & billing practices. It establishes approval authorities, dollar thresholds, timing expectations, and operational steps that Finance, Legal, Procurement, and business owners must follow to ensure accurate financial planning, compliant contracting, timely procurement, and consistent ASC 606-aligned revenue recognition and customer billing.

Purpose and scope:
- Purpose: Provide a single reference for cross-functional processes that materially affect revenue, expense commitments, and controls.
- Scope: Applies to all Redwood business units and customer-facing contracts for Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private products, plus third-party procurement. Excludes employee expense reimbursements (see Expense Reimbursement Policy).

Key principles:
- Segregation of duties: Requestors, approvers, contract owners, and accounting recorders must be distinct where practical.
- Threshold-based approvals: Approvals scale with financial commitment and risk.
- Timely recognition: Revenue recognition follows ASC 606 principles and internal revrec guidance; billing cadence aligns with contract terms.
- Centralization: Material contracts (> $250k total commitment) and capital purchases (> $50k) require centralized review by Finance and Legal.

1) Budgeting & forecasting (quarterly and annual):
Intro: Budgeting sets resource allocations for the upcoming fiscal year; rolling forecasts are updated quarterly to reflect new information.
- Cadence:
  1. Annual budget cycle: initial planning (Aug–Oct), leadership review (Nov), board submission (Dec).
  2. Quarterly rolling forecast: update windows in the middle month of each quarter (e.g., mid-Feb for Q1).
- Owners and responsibilities:
  - Finance: coordinates templates, consolidates, publishes final budgets and forecasts, maintains variance reporting.
  - Product & GTM leads: submit top-down and bottom-up revenue and hiring plans.
  - Engineering and Ops: submit capacity & infra cost forecasts (GPU fleet, cloud spend).
- Requirements & inputs:
  - Revenue: bookings by product (Hosted API, Dedicated, Private) with ARR/MRR, expected churn, and new logo assumptions.
  - Cost: COGS (inference cloud/GPU amortization, egress), Payroll, Hosting, R&D, Sales & Marketing.
  - Capital: planned purchases > $10k listed with vendor and expected delivery quarter.
- Approval matrix (budget items):
  | Item type | Threshold | Required approver(s) | Escalation |
  |-----------|-----------|----------------------|-----------|
  | Dept Opex | <= $250k | Dept Head + Finance BP | VP Finance |
  | Dept Opex | $250k-$1M | Dept Head + VP Finance | CFO |
  | Capital | <= $50k | Dept Head + Finance BP | VP Finance |
  | Capital | $50k-$250k | Dept Head + VP Finance | CFO |
  | Capital | > $250k | Dept Head + CFO + CEO | Board notification |
- Reporting and controls:
  - Monthly variance reports (actual vs budget) published by Finance within 10 business days after month close.
  - Forecast accuracy target: median absolute percentage error (MAPE) <= 10% for consolidated revenue.

2) Contracts & legal process (customer and vendor contracts):
Overview: All customer-facing commercial contracts and vendor Master Services Agreements (MSAs) follow the standard lifecycle: request -> draft -> legal review -> signature -> contract intake.
- Contract classification:
  - Standard Low-Risk (SLR): Redwood standard T&Cs, standard SOW; no custom security addenda, revenue < $250k.
  - Moderate-Risk (MR): Custom terms, limited indemnity changes, revenue $250k–$2M, or Dedicated/Private deployments with specific SLAs.
  - High-Risk (HR): Material custom security/legal requirements, transfer of customer data (sensitive/regulatory), revenue > $2M, or non-standard indemnity/limitation terms.
- Approval matrix (contract signatures):
  | Contract class | Revenue threshold | Legal review | Signature authority |
  |----------------|-------------------|--------------|--------------------|
  | SLR | <= $250k | Optional (Legal template) | Sales Director or above |
  | MR | $250k–$2M | Required | VP Sales + Legal Counsels sign-off |
  | HR | > $2M or sensitive | Required + Security review | CFO + General Counsel |
- Minimum required clauses (customer-facing):
  - Scope of services, deliverables, change control
  - Pricing, billing cadence, payment terms, applicable taxes
  - Data handling and security obligations (reference security-and-compliance controls page)
  - Service levels and credits for Dedicated/Private (if applicable)
  - Intellectual property and license grants
  - Limitation of liability and indemnity clauses (standardized language preferred)
  - Termination for convenience and for cause; post-termination data handling
- Contract intake process (numbered steps):
  1. Sales/Account Executive creates a Contract Intake ticket in the contract queue with customer, expected TCV, and deployment type.
  2. Legal assigns reviewer within 2 business days.
  3. Negotiations tracked via redline with final commercial terms captured in the PSA/SOW.
  4. Countersigned agreements uploaded to Contract Repository (DocID link) and entered into financial systems for invoicing recognition.
- Templates & playbooks:
  - Use standard MSA + SOW templates stored at: /confluence/finance-and-legal/contracts-and-legal-process/templates
  - For Dedicated/Private customers, attach the Deployment and SLA Addendum.

3) Procurement procedures (vendors, capital, and services):
Purpose: Ensure competitive sourcing, cost control, and compliance with contract policy.
- Procurement request flow:
  1. Requestor submits a Purchase Requisition (PR) in the procurement tool with vendor, justification, and estimated total cost.
  2. Procurement reviews supplier history (existing vendor? approved?) and initiates sourcing if needed.
  3. Finance confirms budget availability against departmental budget.
  4. Approver signs PR per thresholds.
- Dollar thresholds & approvals (procurement):
  | Spend type | Threshold | Approvals required |
  |------------|-----------|-------------------|
  | Low (operational) | <= $10k | Dept Manager |
  | Medium | $10k–$50k | Dept Manager + Finance BP |
  | High | $50k–$250k | Dept VP + Procurement lead + Finance |
  | Strategic/Capital | > $250k | Exec sponsor + CFO + Procurement Director |
- Supplier onboarding and controls:
  - New vendors require procurement review, W9 (or local equivalent), and vendor risk assessment for third-party security if they process customer data.
  - Approved vendor list maintained by Procurement; prefer existing contracts/discounts where possible.
- Capital purchases and capitalization policy:
  - Capitalizable assets: servers, GPUs, networking hardware with individual cost >= $10k and useful life > 1 year.
  - Approval required per capital threshold table above; Finance tags POs for capitalization during PO close-out.

4) Revenue recognition & billing policies (overview & examples):
Intro: Revenue recognition follows ASC 606 steps: identify contracts, identify performance obligations, determine transaction price, allocate price to performance obligations, and recognize revenue when (or as) performance obligations are satisfied.
- General rules by product:
  - Hosted API (metered consumption): Recognize revenue over time as usage is delivered; billing typically monthly in arrears. Deferred revenue recognized for prepaid credits and recognized as consumed.
  - Dedicated (reserved capacity): Recognize revenue on a straight-line basis over the term for fixed monthly subscription/commitments. For committed usage with overage, recognize committed portion as service period passes and overage as billed.
  - Private (one-time license + optional services): One-time license fees for perpetual software recognized at point-in-time only when control transfers and all criteria met; managed services or maintenance recognized over the contract period.
- Billing & invoicing standards:
  - Standard payment terms: Net 30 days unless customer credit terms approved by Finance (Net 45/60 for enterprise accounts with documented credit review).
  - Invoicing cadence: monthly by default; annual/quarterly invoices allowed for renewals/enterprise with AR sign-off.
  - Taxes: Sales tax/VAT applied per customer jurisdiction; SalesOps ensures correct tax treatment and collects tax forms for exempt customers.
  - Late payments & collections: Late fee = 1.5% monthly interest after 30 days past due; dunning schedule: 7d reminder, 30d past due notice, 60d escalation to AR + Sales, 90d legal collection escalation.
- Contract modifications & change orders:
  - Material contract modifications (TCV increase > 10% or new performance obligations) require review by Accounting to determine whether to treat as separate contract or modification under ASC 606.
  - Document change orders in SOW Appendix; update revenue schedules in RevRec tracker.
- Deferred revenue & recognition controls:
  - All prepayments and credits must be entered into the billing system and reconciled monthly to the GL.
  - Deferred revenue aging report published monthly; Finance reviews > 90-day deferred balances for proper classification.

5) Operational checklists and templates (quick reference) :
- Contract checklist (minimum fields to capture):
  - Counterparty name; Contract start/end; TCV; Billing frequency; Payment terms; SLA class; Data processing requirements; Legal approver initials; Sales owner.
- Procurement PR checklist: vendor name; vendor tax id; budget code; justification; sourcing notes; approver name(s); expected delivery date.
- Revenue recognition entry checklist: contract id; performance obligations; transaction price; allocation schedule; recognized to date; deferred balance.

6) Escalation & exceptions:
- Exceptions to policy (e.g., expedited purchases, unusually structured deals) must be requested via Exception Request form and approved by: Dept Head + VP Finance + General Counsel (if contractual).
- Escalation path for stuck negotiations: Sales Director -> VP Sales -> General Counsel -> CFO.

7) Ownership, metrics and monitoring:
- Owners:
  - Finance (Revenue Accounting): revenue recognition, deferred revenue, monthly close entries.
  - Legal: contract templates, risk classification, sign-off.
  - Procurement: vendor selection, PO issuance, supplier onboarding.
  - Sales Ops: billing setup, tax handling, contract intake coordination.
- Key metrics to publish monthly:
  - Monthly Recurring Revenue (MRR) and ARR movements (new, expansion, churn)
  - Days Sales Outstanding (DSO) target <= 45 days for self-serve and <= 60 days for enterprise pre-approved terms
  - Forecast accuracy (MAPE) <= 10% consolidated
  - Deferred revenue aging by bucket (0–30d, 31–90d, >90d)

References and templates:
- Contract templates: /confluence/finance-and-legal/contracts-and-legal-process/templates
- Procurement tool guide and approved vendor list: /confluence/finance-and-legal/finance-and-legal-procurement-revrec-guidance-2026.json
- Revenue recognition playbook & RevRec tracker: /confluence/finance-and-legal/revrec-and-billing/revenue-recognition-billing-policy-2026.json

Appendix A — Sample approval request email (Sales to Legal & Finance):
Subject: Contract Approval Request — Acme Corp — $420,000 TCV
Body:
- Customer: Acme Corp
- Product: Dedicated (12-month committed) + onboarding SOW
- TCV: $420,000; Monthly: $35,000
- Requested contract class: Moderate-Risk (Dedicated SLA + custom data addendum)
- Attachments: redline, SOW, security questionnaire
Action requested: Legal review and Finance sign-off for revenue recognition schedule within 3 business days.

Appendix B — Quick decision table (summary):
- New contract TCV <= $250k: Sales Director approval; template preferred; optional Legal.
- New contract $250k–$2M or Dedicated/Private: Legal review required; VP Sales + Legal sign-off.
- New contract > $2M or regulatory data: CFO + General Counsel sign-off; Security review.
